To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the use of color information improves the accuracy of image difference measures in predicting the perceptual quality of images with gamut mapped colors, (b) image difference measures based on image structural similarity are generally superior to measures based on error visibility, and (c) the use of a perceptual color space, such as CIELab, is not sufficient for predicting the perceptual image quality of gamut mapped colors

(1) image difference measures based on structural similarity outperform measures based on error visibility in predicting the quality of images that have undergone gamut mapping, and (2) a measure based on structural similarity that is specifically tailored to predict gamut mapping distortions outperforms all other measures on the gamut mapping dataset.
